frames.narration: A user submits a word count over 8 input splits of 500 words each, with 4 reducers. The coordinator will make one map task per split and one reduce task per partition.
Each map task is sent to a worker that already holds its split on a local disk, so the 4,000 input words are read without crossing the network.
Each mapper counts equal words with its combiner, then puts the counts in 4 buckets by hash of the word modulo 4. Without the combiner 4,000 pairs would be shuffled, and with it only 290.

Each reducer fetches its bucket from every map output. A word always goes to the same reducer, so each total is complete. The reducers get 852, 1,031, 1,245 and 872 words, which add up to the original 4,000.
One map worker is slow: its task has taken 45 time units while the median is 10. At 1.5 times the median, which is 15, the coordinator starts a backup copy on another worker.
The backup finishes after the median time, at 25, and its result is used. The slow original is cancelled. The map phase takes 25 instead of 45.

Now a machine dies. The map outputs of splits 3 and 5 are lost, and so is reducer 2's output. The lineage says exactly which inputs they came from, so the coordinator reruns 2 map tasks and 1 reduce task, not 8 and 4.
Reducers write their totals to the file store. The top words are w00 with 570, w01 with 351 and w02 with 248 out of 39 different words. The coordinator reports the job as done.
